name = "pitzDaily"
dim = 2            # one cell thick, empty front and back
formal_order = 2
refined = "mesh"
grid_sequence = "structured"

[[levels]]
name = "139k"
path = "n139k"

[[levels]]
name = "62k"

file = "postProcessing/pressureDrop/*/multiFieldValue.dat"
column = "Group0"

content.text:
dp is **not** converged, so I can't give a mesh-independent value or an uncertainty. The iterative error is as large as the differences between grids, and the grid trend is non-monotone. I read the numbers by eye from `postProcessing/pressureDrop/0/multiFieldValue.dat` (column Group0) without running a script, so the window means below are approximate.

**1. None of the runs reached a steady state.** All four logs say "SIMPLE solution converged", but only because the `residualControl` limits in `system/fvSolution` are loose (p 1e-2, U and turbulence 1e-3). dp was still moving on every grid when the runs stopped:

| Grid | Samples | dp over the last 10% window | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 279 | about −5.66 to −5.44 | turned around and still rising |
| 28k | 440 | about −4.58 to −4.67 | drifting |
| 62k | 811 | −5.45 → −4.50 | swinging about 1 m²/s² and moving fast at the end |
| 139k | 1419 | −2.97 → −4.06 | falling steadily with no plateau |

On the finest grid, dp changed by about 1.1 m²/s² within the averaging window alone. That run also shows strongly negative "bounding epsilon" values right up to the end, and the relaxation factors are aggressive (0.9 for everything, including p).

**2. The grid sequence doesn't converge.** The approximate window means are:

| Grid | Window mean of dp (m²/s²) |
|---|---|
| 12k | ≈ −5.55 |
| 28k | ≈ −4.65 |
| 62k | ≈ −5.15 |
| 139k | ≈ −3.5 |

The values go up and down from one grid to the next instead of approaching a limit. So Richardson extrapolation and a GCI-type uncertainty estimate aren't valid. Even if they were, those differences are mostly iterative error, not discretisation error.

**To fix it:** tighten `residualControl` by about two orders of magnitude, or stop on a flat dp history. Lower the relaxation factors (for example p 0.3, U and turbulence 0.7), and run each level until dp is flat over the window. Then redo the grid study with the new results.

FINAL: converged=no; value=none; uncertainty=none
